text:
Activation patching provides a stronger diagnostic framework than attention visualization alone. ICLR 2024’s [Towards Best Practices](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042) shows that corruption methods and evaluation metrics can substantially change component-localization conclusions. [Heimersheim and Nanda (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15255) explain interpretation pitfalls: intervention effects depend on the behavior and counterfactual being tested. These results concern language models; transferring them to SASRec requires explicit validation.

Sequential-recommendation research motivates separating item identity from position. [Learning Positional Attention (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.02793) finds learned positional embeddings often encode token distance and proposes directly learned positional relations. [Position-Aware Sequential Attention (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.21052) proposes positional kernels separate from item semantics. These architectural results motivate positional interventions, but do not establish which components support ranking in the four RecHarness categories.

Proposed adaptation: construct paired histories that separately change final-item identity, earlier-item identity, and earlier-item order while preserving padding and length. Patch clean activations into corrupted runs and reverse the direction at item embeddings, positional contributions, attention outputs, and feed-forward outputs. Include unchanged-input patches and matched-random donor/component controls; disable dropout during diagnosis. Measure paired candidate-score margins, target-rank changes, and HR@10, reporting raw effects when normalized recovery denominators approach zero. Prespecify one small training intervention—for example, modest positional-embedding dropout—against baseline and a matched item-embedding-dropout control. Select using the fixed four-category macro validation HR@10. Treat this as a prospective experiment: sensitivity, successful patching, or attention weights alone establish neither an explanation nor improvement.
